:\n" + tagged("file_contents", p, text) and every existing patch target "Original file

:\n" + tagged("original_file", p, text), with the tagged() helper of section 2.2 verbatim; no slice or target text is fenced any more, so remove fenceTag and fencedBlock. The faults, their order and messages, the new-file line, the variants and the inputs digest stay exactly as they are. Write no test file: a probe tests you and the judge patches the example tests. ## Function Compile Card Builds the conversation for one card. Behaviour: generate: one user message per slice file, in sorted path order: the line "Contents of file :", a line break, the opening tag , a line break, the file's text byte for byte (a fence inside it stays as it is) with a line break appended when the text is not empty and does not end in one, then the closing tag and nothing after it; then a user message with the instruction, two line breaks and the output directive. patch: the same, but each target comes first, in targets order: an existing one as the line "Original file :", a line break, , a line break, its text (the same rule) and ; one that does not exist yet as "Target is a new file: it does not exist yet.". No slice or target text is ever put in a fenced block: a fence in a file (a markdown spec, a test of the parser) would pair with the exhibit's own. Variants: N requests with customId .v1..vN and identical messages. A slice file that does not exist is a compile fault, not a silent skip. Steps: - reads: Card - calls: Capture Inputs - produces: Request Examples (the tests must prove each one): 1. given card a, intent generate, slice [docs/B.md, docs/A.md], variants 2; when compiled; then two Requests a.v1 and a.v2; messages[0] is exactly "Contents of file docs/A.md:\n\n# A\n\nAlpha doc.\n", messages[1] the same for docs/B.md ("# B\n\nBeta doc.\n"), messages[2] "Write src/a.ts.\n\n" + the directive (ref: tests/fixtures/compiler/cards/generateA.json (the card), tests/fixtures/compiler/project (the root)) 2. given card p, intent patch, targets [src/x.ts] which exists with 3 lines, slice [docs/A.md]; when compiled; then the first message is exactly "Original file src/x.ts:\n\nexport const x = 1;\nexport const y = 2;\nexport const z = 3;\n" (132 chars), the second the tagged docs/A.md (ref: tests/fixtures/compiler/cards/patchP.json (the card), tests/fixtures/compiler/project (the root)) 3. given a slice naming docs/missing.md; when compiled; then a compile fault naming docs/missing.md; no Request 4. given card f, intent generate, targets [src/f.ts], slice [docs/F.md]; docs/F.md is "# F\n\n```ts\nconst f = 1;\n```" (no final newline); when compiled; then messages[0] is exactly "Contents of file docs/F.md:\n\n# F\n\n```ts\nconst f = 1;\n```\n" (the fence kept, one newline added); no message holds a line that is only "```md" (ref: tests/fixtures/compiler/cards/fencedF.json (the card), tests/fixtures/compiler/project/docs/F.md) 5. given card n, intent patch, targets [src/x.ts, src/z.ts], src/z.ts absent, no slice; when compiled; then three messages: the tagged original of src/x.ts (as example 2), "Target src/z.ts is a new file: it does not exist yet.", then the instruction + directive (ref: tests/fixtures/compiler/cards/patchNew.json) Data Card: One unit of work for an executor; what morph run compiles into a request. Schema: { "customId": "string, ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$", "intent": "'generate' | 'patch'", "targets": "string[] non-empty, repo-relative, distinct after normalisation", "contextSlice": "string[] default []", "instruction": "string non-empty", "acceptance": "string | null — a shell command run from the repo root", "model": "string | null", "maxTokens": "number | null", "reasoning": "{ maxTokens: number } | { effort: 'low'|'medium'|'high' } | null", "variants": "number >= 1, default 1", "dependsOn": "string[] default []" } Data Request: One provider-neutral chat request. Schema: { "customId": "string — '.v'", "model": "string | null", "maxTokens": "number | null", "reasoning": "Card.reasoning", "messages": "{ role: 'system'|'user'|'assistant', content: string }[]" } ## Component requirements / guardrails Requirements: - Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit. - One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr. - Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response and Stub Answer are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation (P4). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). - Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~. No `any`: use `unknown` and narrow. Tests are vitest: `toBe` on scalars and short strings, `toStrictEqual` on a whole result; stubs come from `tests/helpers.ts`, never your own.

Patch two files (their current texts follow); change nothing else in them. src/runloop/types.ts: RunDeps gains `acceptanceTimeoutMs?: number` as its last member. src/runloop/generation.ts: import DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS from "../acceptance/run.js" and pass verifyCard `timeoutMs: deps.acceptanceTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (never deps.config.timeoutMs); export `stageCount(log: string): number`, the number of lines of log.split("\n") that start with "== "; a rejected card's retry context comes from the variant whose acceptance ran (diff !== null) with the greatest stageCount(log), a tie going to the LATER variant (see the table of section 2.2). The outcome (acceptanceLog = the last variant's log, earlierFailures) and every other rule stay exactly as they are. Write no test file: a probe tests you and the judge patches the example tests.

## Function Process Generation

compile → send → parse → verify per card; a compile fault or stale inputs discard the answer; accepted cards fire the commit hook.

Behaviour: processGeneration(cards, deps, root) compiles every card with compileCard, keeping each card's input digest; sends all variants of all cards in ONE sendGeneration(deps.config, requests, deps.transport) call (so deps.config's concurrency pools across the whole generation) and slices answers and usage back to each card by request index; then verifies each card in input order. Per card: a compile fault → {status: "failed", reason "compile: <first fault message>", acceptanceLog = the fault messages joined by "\n"}; else recompute the digest (captureInputs) and compareCaptures against the compile digest — a non-empty change → {status: "failed", reason "stale inputs", acceptanceLog "stale inputs: <changed paths, comma+space joined>"} and no acceptance is run; else build one VariantAnswer per variant (variant id "<customId>.v<n>"; a null-text answer becomes {corrupt: the answer's error ?? "no text returned"}, else parseAnswer(text, targets)) and call verifyCard with timeoutMs = deps.acceptanceTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (300000, Run Acceptance's default) — the acceptance has its own timeout, never the processor's HTTP deps.config.timeoutMs. Accepted → {status: "written", winningVariant = the accepted variant id, acceptanceLog = the winner's log, earlierFailures = the logs of the rejected variants tried before it, commit = the sha from deps.commit(customId, targets), diffstat from the hook}; no variant accepted → {status: "failed", reason "acceptance failed", acceptanceLog = the last variant's log, earlierFailures = the earlier variants' logs, commit null, diffstat null}. attempts is 1 for every outcome of one round. Returns {outcomes, usage, requests, retryContexts}: usage is the Usage of every request sent; requests is one Request Usage per request sent, in send order ({customId: the request id, model: the request's model ?? deps.config.model, provider, generationId, inputTokens, outputTokens, cost from its Usage, finishReason and error from its Answer}); retryContexts holds one Retry Context per FAILED outcome, keyed by its customId, in outcome order, and nothing for a written card. A compile fault or stale inputs → {acceptanceOutput: the outcome's acceptanceLog, previousDiff: null}. A rejected card → of the variants whose acceptance ran (the verify result's diff is not null), the one that got FURTHEST gives {acceptanceOutput: its log, previousDiff: its diff, "" when the attempt changed nothing}: furthest = the greatest stageCount(log), a tie → the later variant; stageCount(log) (exported) is the number of lines of the log, split on "\n", that begin with "== " (the stage headers the acceptance prints: == tsc, == probe, …). When no variant ran (every answer corrupt or truncated) → {acceptanceOutput: the last result's log, previousDiff: null}. The log and the diff of the retry always come from the same attempt, and previousDiff is null exactly when no acceptance ran. The outcome's acceptanceLog and earlierFailures do not change (the last variant's log, the earlier ones').

Steps:
- uses: compiler
- uses: processor
- uses: acceptance
- produces: Card Outcome
- produces: Request Usage
- produces: Retry Context

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a stub config (answersDir a tmp root with a.v1.md and b.v1.md, each a fenced ts block); cards [a → out/a.ts, b → out/b.ts], each acceptance passes when its file holds the marker; a recording commit hook; when processed; then outcomes a and b both status "written", winningVariant "a.v1"/"b.v1", attempts 1, commit set; the commit hook fired twice; usage length 2 (provider "stub" for each)
2. given a stub config; one card whose written file does NOT satisfy its acceptance (acceptance "exit 1"); when processed; then one outcome status "failed", reason "acceptance failed", winningVariant null, commit null; the commit hook did not fire
3. given a stub config; cards [a → shared.ts, b] where b.contextSlice holds shared.ts and a (processed first) is accepted and writes shared.ts; when processed; then a status "written"; b status "failed", reason "stale inputs", acceptanceLog beginning "stale inputs: shared.ts"; b's acceptance was never run
4. given a stub config; out/a.ts holds 'export const x = "OLD";\n'; card a → out/a.ts, variants 2, acceptance 'grep -q PASS out/a.ts || { echo "red: $(cat out/a.ts)"; exit 1; }'; a.v1.md a fenced ts block holding 'export const x = "ONE";\n'; a.v2.md the text '```ts\nexport const x = 2;\n' (one fence line: truncated); when processed; then outcome a status "failed", reason "acceptance failed", acceptanceLog TRUNCATED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE (Verify Card), earlierFailures ['red: export const x = "ONE";\n']; retryContexts {a: {acceptanceOutput: 'red: export const x = "ONE";\n', previousDiff: '--- a/out/a.ts\n+++ b/out/a.ts\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-export const x = "OLD";\n+export const x = "ONE";\n'}} (the variant that ran, not the last one); out/a.ts holds 'export const x = "OLD";\n' again
5. given as example 4, but a.v2.md a fenced ts block holding 'export const x = "TWO";\n'; when processed; then outcome a status "failed", acceptanceLog 'red: export const x = "TWO";\n', earlierFailures ['red: export const x = "ONE";\n']; retryContexts {a: {acceptanceOutput: 'red: export const x = "TWO";\n', previousDiff: '--- a/out/a.ts\n+++ b/out/a.ts\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-export const x = "OLD";\n+export const x = "TWO";\n'}} (both ran, no stage header in either: the tie goes to the later one)
6. given a stub config; cards [a → out/a.ts (a.v1.md fenced, its acceptance passes), b → out/b.ts (b.v1.md the text '```ts\nexport const x = 2;\n'), c → out/c.ts with contextSlice [docs/missing.md], which does not exist], variants 1 each; when processed; then a "written"; b and c "failed"; retryContexts exactly {b: {acceptanceOutput: TRUNCATED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE, previousDiff: null}, c: {acceptanceOutput: "contextSlice 'docs/missing.md' does not exist", previousDiff: null}} (no entry for a)
7. given a stub config (model "stub"); cards [a → out/a.ts with model null, b → out/b.ts with model "glm-x"], variants 1, both accepted; when processed; then requests [{customId: "a.v1", model: "stub", provider: "stub", generationId: "stub-a.v1", inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, cost: 0, finishReason: "stop", error: null}, {customId: "b.v1", model: "glm-x", provider: "stub", generationId: "stub-b.v1", inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, cost: 0, finishReason: "stop", error: null}]; retryContexts {}
8. given a stub config; out/a.ts holds 'export const x = "ONE";\n'; card a → out/a.ts, variants 1, acceptance 'grep -q PASS out/a.ts || { echo "red: $(cat out/a.ts)"; exit 1; }'; a.v1.md a fenced ts block holding 'export const x = "ONE";\n' (the file unchanged); when processed; then outcome a status "failed", acceptanceLog 'red: export const x = "ONE";\n'; retryContexts {a: {acceptanceOutput: 'red: export const x = "ONE";\n', previousDiff: ""}} (the acceptance ran on an attempt that changed nothing: the empty diff, not null)
9. given a stub config; out/a.ts holds 'export const x = "OLD";\n'; card a → out/a.ts, variants 2, acceptance "grep -q ONE out/a.ts && { echo '== tsc'; echo '== probe'; echo 'red: one'; exit 1; }; echo '== tsc'; echo 'red: two'; exit 1"; a.v1.md a fenced ts block holding 'export const x = "ONE";\n', a.v2.md one holding 'export const x = "TWO";\n'; when processed; then outcome a status "failed", acceptanceLog "== tsc\nred: two\n", earlierFailures ["== tsc\n== probe\nred: one\n"]; retryContexts {a: {acceptanceOutput: "== tsc\n== probe\nred: one\n", previousDiff: '--- a/out/a.ts\n+++ b/out/a.ts\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-export const x = "OLD";\n+export const x = "ONE";\n'}} (v1 reached 2 stages, v2 1: the furthest, not the last); stageCount of the two logs 2 and 1, of "" 0, of "a == b\n" 0
10. given a stub config whose timeoutMs (the processor's HTTP timeout) is 100; deps without acceptanceTimeoutMs; card a → out/a.ts, acceptance "sleep 1; grep -q PASS out/a.ts"; a.v1.md a fenced ts block holding 'export const x = "PASS";\n'; when processed; then outcome a status "written", winningVariant "a.v1" — the acceptance ran under its own default of 300000 ms, not the config's 100 ms
11. given a stub config with timeoutMs 600000 and deps.acceptanceTimeoutMs 200; card a → out/a.ts, acceptance "sleep 30"; a.v1.md a fenced ts block; when processed; then outcome a status "failed", reason "acceptance failed", its acceptanceLog holding "acceptance timed out after 200 ms"; the commit hook did not fire

Data Card Outcome: How one card ended in a run.
Schema:
{ customId: string, status: 'written'|'failed'|'skipped'|'budget-exceeded', reason: string | null, attempts: number, winningVariant: string | null, acceptanceLog: string, earlierFailures: string[], commit: string | null, diffstat: { files: number, insertions: number, deletions: number } | null }

Data Request Usage: One request a run sent, as the processor answered it (one row per variant, retries included).
Schema:
{ customId: string, model: string, provider: string | null, generationId: string | null, inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, cost: number | null, finishReason: string | null, error: string | null }

Data Retry Context: What the retry of a failed card is told — the acceptance output and the diff of the same failed attempt.
Schema:
{ acceptanceOutput: string, previousDiff: string | null } — previousDiff is the diff of an attempt whose acceptance ran ("" when it changed nothing), null when no acceptance ran

## Component requirements / guardrails

- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response and Stub Answer are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation (P4). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).

## Function Verify Card

Best-of-N over the parsed variants.

Behaviour: verifyCard({root, targets, command, variants, env, timeoutMs}) snapshots the targets once, then for each variant in order: a corrupt answer gives the stand-in result {exit null, log "answer corrupt: <reason>", diff null} and a truncated one {exit null, log TRUNCATED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE, diff null}, nothing written; TRUNCATED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE (exported) is the old runner's three sentences, exactly "The previous answer was cut off mid-file: it opened a ``` code fence and never closed it, so the file body could not be extracted. Answer again with the COMPLETE file, and close the fence." (one line, single spaces; it is what the retry of a cut-off card is told); otherwise every file of the answer is written under root and the acceptance is run; exit 0 → that variant is accepted, its files stay, its result has diff null and no later variant is tried; any other exit → the result carries the Build Attempt Diff of the written files against the snapshot, the snapshot is restored, and the next variant is tried. Returns Verify Outcome; with no green variant accepted is null and the tree equals the snapshot.

Steps:
- reads: Parsed Answer
- calls: Snapshot Targets
- calls: Run Acceptance
- calls: Build Attempt Diff
- produces: Verify Outcome

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given root with src/a.ts = "old\n"; targets [src/a.ts]; command `grep good src/a.ts || { echo "FAIL: no good in src/a.ts"; exit 1; }`; variants c.v1 {corrupt: "missing section for src/a.ts"}, c.v2 {files: {src/a.ts: "bad\n"}}, c.v3 {files: {src/a.ts: "good\n"}}; when verified; then accepted {variant: "c.v3"}; results [{c.v1, exit null, log "answer corrupt: missing section for src/a.ts", diff null}, {c.v2, exit 1, log "FAIL: no good in src/a.ts\n", diff "--- a/src/a.ts\n+++ b/src/a.ts\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-old\n+bad\n"}, {c.v3, exit 0, log "good\n", diff null}]; src/a.ts reads "good\n"
2. given the same root and command; targets [src/a.ts, src/b.ts], src/b.ts absent; variants c.v1 {truncated: true}, c.v2 {files: {src/a.ts: "bad\n", src/b.ts: "x\n"}}; when verified; then accepted null; results [{c.v1, exit null, log TRUNCATED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE, diff null}, {c.v2, exit 1, log "FAIL: no good in src/a.ts\n", diff "--- a/src/a.ts\n+++ b/src/a.ts\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-old\n+bad\n--- /dev/null\n+++ b/src/b.ts\n@@ -0,0 +1,1 @@\n+x\n"}]; src/a.ts reads "old\n" and src/b.ts does not exist
3. given the same root, command and targets [src/a.ts]; variants c.v1 {files: {src/a.ts: "good\n"}}, c.v2 {files: {src/a.ts: "good\n"}}; when verified; then accepted {variant: "c.v1"}; results has exactly one entry, c.v1 with exit 0: c.v2 is never run
4. given the exported TRUNCATED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE; when read; then "The previous answer was cut off mid-file: it opened a ``` code fence and never closed it, so the file body could not be extracted. Answer again with the COMPLETE file, and close the fence." (188 chars); it holds no "answer truncated"

Data Parsed Answer: The outcome of Parse Answer.
Schema:
{ files: { [path: string]: string } } | { corrupt: string } | { truncated: true }

Data Verify Outcome: The result of best-of-N verification of one card.
Schema:
{ accepted: { variant: string } | null, results: { variant: string, exit: number | null, log: string, diff: string | null }[] }

## Function Run Deck

Generations in order (layerGenerations), budget checked at each generation boundary (maxCards, deadline), retries budgeted per card (2) and capped per generation (maxRetryBatches), the Run Report produced at the end.

Behaviour: runDeck(input, deps) runs input.deck generation by generation in the order of layerGenerations(input.deck). At each generation boundary it checks the budget: deps.now() >= input.budget.deadline → every not-yet-done card of this and the later generations becomes {status: "budget-exceeded", reason "deadline"}; cardsProcessed >= input.budget.maxCards → reason "maxCards <maxCards>". Otherwise it resolves the runnable cards (resolveRunnable with the statuses so far), records the skipped outcomes, runs processGeneration on the runnable cards, accumulates their usage and request rows, keeps the Retry Context of every failed card (by its original id; a later round's context replaces an earlier one), and adds the runnable count to cardsProcessed. A card that failed is retried: the budget is per card — every card may be retried 2 times, in whichever generation it runs — and input.budget.maxRetryBatches caps the retry batches of ONE generation: retryBatches starts at 0 at every generation, and while some failed card of this generation has been retried fewer than 2 times and retryBatches < maxRetryBatches, a retry batch runs (retryBatches += 1) for all such cards: buildRetry(original card, retryNumber, the card's latest Retry Context acceptanceOutput, its previousDiff) for each — so the retry carries the output and the diff of the same failed attempt — processGeneration on the retries, and a retry that is written updates the card's outcome (status "written", its commit, attempts = the retry number + 1) while every attempt's log is appended to earlierFailures. At the end it builds the Run Report: runId, completedAt = deps.now(), branch = input.branch, processor = deps.config.id, generations = the generation count, outcomes in deck order, usageTotals {inputTokens, outputTokens summed; cost the sum of the reported costs or null when none was reported; requests = the number of usage rows}, requests = every Request Usage row of every processGeneration call of the run, in send order. Returns {report, outcomes}. It writes and commits nothing: the archive is P6 git's.

Steps:
- calls: Resolve Runnable
- calls: Process Generation
- calls: Build Retry
- reads: Retry Context
- produces: Run Report

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response and Stub Answer are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation (P4). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Callee Resolve Runnable: A card whose dependency failed, was skipped or ran out of budget is skipped with the reason naming that dependency.
Behaviour: resolveRunnable(cards, done) takes the cards of one generation and `done`, a Record of the final status of every card processed so far (written | failed | skipped | budget-exceeded). A card is skipped when any id in its dependsOn has a status in `done` other than "written"; its reason is "dependency <id> <status>" for the FIRST such dependency in dependsOn order. A dependency absent from `done` (external, or satisfied outside the run) is ignored. Returns {runnable: Card[], skipped: CardOutcome[]} keeping the input order; a skipped card's outcome is {status: "skipped", reason, attempts 0, winningVariant null, acceptanceLog "", earlierFailures [], commit null, diffstat null}.

Callee Process Generation: compile → send → parse → verify per card; a compile fault or stale inputs discard the answer; accepted cards fire the commit hook.
Behaviour: processGeneration(cards, deps, root) compiles every card with compileCard, keeping each card's input digest; sends all variants of all cards in ONE sendGeneration(deps.config, requests, deps.transport) call (so deps.config's concurrency pools across the whole generation) and slices answers and usage back to each card by request index; then verifies each card in input order. Per card: a compile fault → {status: "failed", reason "compile: <first fault message>", acceptanceLog = the fault messages joined by "\n"}; else recompute the digest (captureInputs) and compareCaptures against the compile digest — a non-empty change → {status: "failed", reason "stale inputs", acceptanceLog "stale inputs: <changed paths, comma+space joined>"} and no acceptance is run; else build one VariantAnswer per variant (variant id "<customId>.v<n>"; a null-text answer becomes {corrupt: the answer's error ?? "no text returned"}, else parseAnswer(text, targets)) and call verifyCard with timeoutMs = deps.acceptanceTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (300000, Run Acceptance's default) — the acceptance has its own timeout, never the processor's HTTP deps.config.timeoutMs. Accepted → {status: "written", winningVariant = the accepted variant id, acceptanceLog = the winner's log, earlierFailures = the logs of the rejected variants tried before it, commit = the sha from deps.commit(customId, targets), diffstat from the hook}; no variant accepted → {status: "failed", reason "acceptance failed", acceptanceLog = the last variant's log, earlierFailures = the earlier variants' logs, commit null, diffstat null}. attempts is 1 for every outcome of one round. Returns {outcomes, usage, requests, retryContexts}: usage is the Usage of every request sent; requests is one Request Usage per request sent, in send order ({customId: the request id, model: the request's model ?? deps.config.model, provider, generationId, inputTokens, outputTokens, cost from its Usage, finishReason and error from its Answer}); retryContexts holds one Retry Context per FAILED outcome, keyed by its customId, in outcome order, and nothing for a written card. A compile fault or stale inputs → {acceptanceOutput: the outcome's acceptanceLog, previousDiff: null}. A rejected card → of the variants whose acceptance ran (the verify result's diff is not null), the one that got FURTHEST gives {acceptanceOutput: its log, previousDiff: its diff, "" when the attempt changed nothing}: furthest = the greatest stageCount(log), a tie → the later variant; stageCount(log) (exported) is the number of lines of the log, split on "\n", that begin with "== " (the stage headers the acceptance prints: == tsc, == probe, …). When no variant ran (every answer corrupt or truncated) → {acceptanceOutput: the last result's log, previousDiff: null}. The log and the diff of the retry always come from the same attempt, and previousDiff is null exactly when no acceptance ran. The outcome's acceptanceLog and earlierFailures do not change (the last variant's log, the earlier ones').

Callee Build Retry: The retry card <base>.r<n> carrying the acceptance command, its output and the previous attempt diff, or the word that the answer was discarded unread; at most 2 retries per card; Run Deck caps the retry batches of each generation.
Behaviour: buildRetry(card, attempt, acceptanceOutput, previousDiff) returns a NEW Card. attempt must be 1 or 2, else it throws Error "buildRetry: attempt must be 1 or 2". The base id is card.customId with a trailing ".r<digits>" removed; the new customId is "<base>.r<attempt>". intent, targets, contextSlice, acceptance, model, maxTokens, reasoning and variants are copied from `card`; dependsOn is []. previousDiff null means the acceptance never ran (the answer was discarded unread, the card did not compile or its inputs went stale); a string, "" included, means it ran. instruction = card.instruction + "\n\n<acceptance_output>\n" + header + "\n" + acceptanceOutput + "\n</acceptance_output>\n" + closing, where it ran → header "A previous attempt failed its acceptance check (`" + (card.acceptance ?? "") + "`):" and closing "Please fix the issues and produce the complete corrected file."; previousDiff null → header "A previous attempt was discarded before acceptance could run:" and closing "Produce the complete file again, from the context given above.". When previousDiff is a non-empty string, + "\n\n<previous_attempt_diff>\nYour previous attempt changed the file like this (unified diff):\n" + previousDiff + "\n</previous_attempt_diff>\nThe diff above is YOUR OWN previous edit, not a proposed change: correct it where it went wrong rather than rewriting the file from scratch."
